sanskrit: dhanuḥ praharaṇaṃ śreṣṭham iti vādaḥ pitāmaha matas tu mama dharmajña khaḍga eva susaṃśitaḥ
english: There is a saying, grandfather, that the bow is the finest of weapons; yet my own view, O knower of dharma, is that the keen-honed sword is best of all.

sanskrit: viśīrṇe kārmuke rājan prakṣīṇeṣu ca vājiṣu khaḍgena śakyate yuddhe sādhv ātmā parirakṣitum
english: When the bow has been shattered, O king, and the horses have all been spent, with the sword a warrior may still guard himself well in battle.

sanskrit: śarāsanadharāṃś caiva gadāśaktidharāṃs tathā ekaḥ khaḍgadharo vīraḥ samarthaḥ pratibādhitum
english: Bearers of the bow, and those who wield mace and spear alike — a single hero armed with the sword is able to hold them all at bay.

sanskrit: atra me saṃśayaś caiva kautūhalam atīva ca kiṃ svit praharaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvayuddheṣu pārthiva
english: On this point I have both a doubt and the keenest curiosity: which weapon, O king, is the finest in every kind of combat?

sanskrit: kathaṃ cotpāditaḥ khaḍgaḥ kasyārthāya ca kena vā pūrvācāryaṃ ca khaḍgasya prabrūhi prapitāmaha
english: And how was the sword brought into being, for whose sake, and by whom? Tell me too, great-grandfather, who was the first teacher of the sword.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā mādrīputrasya dhīmataḥ sarvakauśalasaṃyuktaṃ sūkṣmacitrārthavac chubham
english: When he had heard this speech of the wise son of Mādrī — a speech full of all skill, fair, and rich with subtle and striking meaning —

sanskrit: tatas tasyottaraṃ vākyaṃ svaravarṇopapāditam śikṣānyāyopasaṃpannaṃ droṇaśiṣyāya pṛcchate
english: then, in reply to the disciple of Droṇa who had asked, he framed an answer well-formed in accent and articulation, perfect in learning and reasoning.

sanskrit: uvāca sarvadharmajño dhanurvedasya pāragaḥ śaratalpagato bhīṣmo nakulāya mahātmane
english: Bhīṣma, knower of all dharma and master of the science of arms, lying upon his bed of arrows, spoke to the great-souled Nakula.

sanskrit: tattvaṃ śṛṇuṣva mādreya yad etat paripṛcchasi prabodhito 'smi bhavatā dhātumān iva parvataḥ
english: "Hear the truth, son of Mādrī, concerning all that you ask; by you I am roused, as a mountain rich in ore is wakened to its veins."

sanskrit: salilaikārṇavaṃ tāta purā sarvam abhūd idam niṣprakampam anākāśam anirdeśyamahītalam
english: "Of old, dear child, all this was a single ocean of water, unstirred, without sky, its floor of earth beyond all designation."

sanskrit: tamaḥsaṃvṛtam asparśam atigambhīradarśanam niḥśabdaṃ cāprameyaṃ ca tatra jajñe pitāmahaḥ
english: "Wrapped in darkness, untouchable, fathomless to the gaze, soundless and immeasurable — and within it the Grandsire was born."

sanskrit: so 'sṛjad vāyum agniṃ ca bhāskaraṃ cāpi vīryavān ākāśam asṛjac cordhvam adho bhūmiṃ ca nairṛtim
english: "He, the mighty one, created wind and fire and the radiant sun; he created the sky above, and below the earth in its southwestern quarter."

sanskrit: nabhaḥ sacandratāraṃ ca nakṣatrāṇi grahāṃs tathā saṃvatsarān ahorātrān ṛtūn atha lavān kṣaṇān
english: "The heavens with their moon and stars, the lunar mansions and the planets, the years, the days and nights, the seasons, the moments and the instants —"

sanskrit: tataḥ śarīraṃ lokasthaṃ sthāpayitvā pitāmahaḥ janayām āsa bhagavān putrān uttamatejasaḥ
english: "then, having set his own body within the world, the blessed Grandsire begot sons of surpassing splendour."

sanskrit: marīcim ṛṣim atriṃ ca pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum vasiṣṭhāṅgirasau cobhau rudraṃ ca prabhum īśvaram
english: "The seer Marīci, and Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, both Vasiṣṭha and Aṅgiras, and Rudra the mighty lord —"

sanskrit: prācetasas tathā dakṣaḥ kanyāḥ ṣaṣṭim ajījanat tā vai brahmarṣayaḥ sarvāḥ prajārthaṃ pratipedire
english: "and Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, who begot sixty daughters; and all those brahmin-seers received them for the sake of progeny."

sanskrit: tābhyo viśvāni bhūtāni devāḥ pitṛgaṇās tathā gandharvāpsarasaś caiva rakṣāṃsi vividhāni ca
english: "From them sprang all beings: the gods and the hosts of the ancestors, the gandharvas and apsarases, and demons of many kinds —"

sanskrit: patatrimṛgamīnāś ca plavaṃgāś ca mahoragāḥ nānākṛtibalāś cānye jalakṣitivicāriṇaḥ
english: "birds, beasts and fishes, monkeys and great serpents, and others of varied form and strength that move through water and over the land."

sanskrit: audbhidāḥ svedajāś caiva aṇḍajāś ca jarāyujāḥ jajñe tāta tathā sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: "Sprung from the soil, born of sweat, born of eggs and born of the womb — thus, dear child, came forth the whole world, moving and unmoving alike."

sanskrit: bhūtasargam imaṃ kṛtvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ śāśvataṃ vedapaṭhitaṃ dharmaṃ ca yuyuje punaḥ
english: "Having wrought this creation of beings, the Grandsire of all the worlds then ordained as well the eternal dharma that the Vedas proclaim."

sanskrit: tasmin dharme sthitā devāḥ sahācāryapurohitāḥ ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sasādhyā marudaśvinaḥ
english: "Established in that dharma stood the gods together with their teachers and priests: the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sādhyas, the Maruts and the Aśvins —"

sanskrit: bhṛgvatryaṅgirasaḥ siddhāḥ kāśyapaś ca tapodhanaḥ vasiṣṭhagautamāgastyās tathā nāradaparvatau
english: "Bhṛgu, Atri and Aṅgiras, the Siddhas, and Kaśyapa rich in austerity, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama and Agastya, and Nārada and Parvata too."

sanskrit: ṛṣayo vālakhilyāś ca prabhāsāḥ sikatās tathā ghṛtācāḥ somavāyavyā vaikhānasamarīcipāḥ
english: "The seers, the Vālakhilyas, the Prabhāsas and the Sikatās, the Ghṛtācas, those born of Soma and of the wind, the Vaikhānasas and the Marīcipas —"

sanskrit: akṛṣṭāś caiva haṃsāś ca ṛṣayo 'thāgniyonijāḥ vānaprasthāḥ pṛśnayaś ca sthitā brahmānuśāsane
english: "the Akṛṣṭas and the Haṃsas, the seers born of the womb of fire, the forest hermits and the Pṛśnis — all abode within the rule of Brahmā."

sanskrit: dānavendrās tv atikramya tat pitāmahaśāsanam dharmasyāpacayaṃ cakruḥ krodhalobhasamanvitāḥ
english: "But the lords of the dānavas, transgressing that ordinance of the Grandsire, wrought the decay of dharma, possessed by wrath and greed."

sanskrit: hiraṇyakaśipuś caiva hiraṇyākṣo virocanaḥ śambaro vipracittiś ca prahrādo namucir baliḥ
english: "Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa, Virocana, Śambara and Vipracitti, Prahrāda, Namuci and Bali —"

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ sagaṇā daityadānavāḥ dharmasetum atikramya remire 'dharmaniścayāḥ
english: "these and many others, daityas and dānavas with their hordes, broke through the dyke of dharma and revelled, resolved upon unrighteousness."

sanskrit: sarve sma tulyajātīyā yathā devās tathā vayam ity evaṃ hetum āsthāya spardhamānāḥ surarṣibhiḥ
english: "'We are all of one birth: as the gods are, so are we' — taking their stand on such a claim, they contended with the gods and the seers."

sanskrit: na priyaṃ nāpy anukrośaṃ cakrur bhūteṣu bhārata trīn upāyān atikramya daṇḍena rurudhuḥ prajāḥ na jagmuḥ saṃvidaṃ taiś ca darpād asurasattamāḥ
english: "They showed neither kindness nor compassion toward living beings, O Bhārata; passing over the three milder means, they oppressed the people with the rod alone, and in their arrogance those foremost of asuras would make no compact with them."

sanskrit: atha vai bhagavān brahmā brahmarṣibhir upasthitaḥ tadā himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe suramye padmatārake
english: "Then the blessed Brahmā, attended by the brahmin-seers, upon the most lovely ridge of Himavat, jewelled with lotuses and stars,"

sanskrit: śatayojanavistāre maṇimuktācayācite tasmin girivare putra puṣpitadrumakānane tasthau sa vibudhaśreṣṭho brahmā lokārthasiddhaye
english: "a hundred yojanas in breadth, heaped with gems and pearls — upon that noblest of mountains, my son, with its forests of flowering trees, Brahmā, foremost of the wise, took his stand to accomplish the welfare of the worlds."

sanskrit: tato varṣasahasrānte vitānam akarot prabhuḥ vidhinā kalpadṛṣṭena yathoktenopapāditam
english: "Then, at the close of a thousand years, the Lord spread out the sacrificial canopy, ordered by the rite revealed in the scriptures and furnished just as enjoined."

sanskrit: ṛṣibhir yajñapaṭubhir yathāvat karmakartṛbhiḥ marudbhiḥ parisaṃstīrṇaṃ dīpyamānaiś ca pāvakaiḥ
english: "By seers skilled in sacrifice, who duly performed each rite, by the Maruts spread all about, and by the blazing fires,"

sanskrit: kāñcanair yajñabhāṇḍaiś ca bhrājiṣṇubhir alaṃkṛtam vṛtaṃ devagaṇaiś caiva prababhau yajñamaṇḍalam
english: "adorned with shining golden vessels of sacrifice, and ringed about by the hosts of gods, the sacrificial enclosure shone resplendent."

sanskrit: tathā brahmarṣibhiś caiva sadasyair upaśobhitam tatra ghoratamaṃ vṛttam ṛṣīṇāṃ me pariśrutam
english: "Graced too by brahmin-seers serving as members of the assembly — and there, so I have heard from the seers, a most dreadful thing took place."

sanskrit: candramā vimalaṃ vyoma yathābhyuditatārakam vidāryāgniṃ tathā bhūtam utthitaṃ śrūyate tataḥ
english: "As the moon and the rising stars adorn the cloudless sky, so, it is told, a being then rose up, rending the fire of the altar."

sanskrit: nīlotpalasavarṇābhaṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ kṛśodaram prāṃśu durdarśanaṃ caivāpy atitejas tathaiva ca
english: "Of hue like the blue lotus, with sharp fangs and lean of belly, tall and terrible to behold, and of surpassing brilliance withal —"

sanskrit: tasminn utpatamāne ca pracacāla vasuṃdharā tatrormikalilāvartaś cukṣubhe ca mahārṇavaḥ
english: "as that being sprang forth, the earth trembled, and the great ocean was churned into a turmoil of waves and whirlpools."

sanskrit: petur ulkā mahotpātāḥ śākhāś ca mumucur drumāḥ aprasannā diśaḥ sarvāḥ pavanaś cāśivo vavau muhur muhuś ca bhūtāni prāvyathanta bhayāt tathā
english: "Meteors fell as great portents, the trees shed their boughs, all the quarters grew overcast, an evil wind blew, and again and again living creatures trembled with terror."

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ dṛṣṭvā tad adbhutam upasthitam maharṣisuragandharvān uvācedaṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: "Then, beholding that wondrous and tumultuous thing arisen before him, the Grandsire spoke thus to the great seers, the gods and the gandharvas:"

sanskrit: mayaitac cintitaṃ bhūtam asir nāmaiṣa vīryavān rakṣaṇārthāya lokasya vadhāya ca suradviṣām
english: "'This being have I conceived; it is the Sword, mighty by name and nature, fashioned for the protection of the world and the slaying of the foes of the gods.'"

sanskrit: tatas tad rūpam utsṛjya babhau nistriṃśa eva saḥ vimalas tīkṣṇadhāraś ca kālāntaka ivodyataḥ
english: "Then, casting off that form, it shone forth as a sword indeed — bright, keen-edged, and uplifted like Death, the ender of time."

sanskrit: tatas taṃ śitikaṇṭhāya rudrāyarṣabhaketave brahmā dadāv asiṃ dīptam adharmaprativāraṇam
english: "Then to the blue-throated Rudra, whose banner bears the bull, Brahmā gave that blazing sword, the warding-off of unrighteousness."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān rudro brahmarṣigaṇasaṃstutaḥ pragṛhyāsim ameyātmā rūpam anyac cakāra ha
english: "Then the blessed Rudra, praised by the hosts of brahmin-seers, the immeasurable one, grasped the sword and took on another form."

sanskrit: caturbāhuḥ spṛśan mūrdhnā bhūsthito 'pi nabhastalam ūrdhvadṛṣṭir mahāliṅgo mukhāj jvālāḥ samutsṛjan vikurvan bahudhā varṇān nīlapāṇḍuralohitān
english: "Four-armed, though standing upon the earth he touched the vault of heaven with his head, his gaze turned upward, of mighty emblem, casting forth flames from his mouth and shifting his colour through many hues — blue, pale, and red."

sanskrit: bibhrat kṛṣṇājinaṃ vāso hemapravaratārakam netraṃ caikaṃ lalāṭena bhāskarapratimaṃ mahat śuśubhāte ca vimale dve netre kṛṣṇapiṅgale
english: "Wearing a black antelope-skin as his garment, starred with choice gold, with one great eye set in his forehead like the sun, while his two other eyes shone clear, black and tawny."

sanskrit: tato devo mahādevaḥ śūlapāṇir bhagākṣihā saṃpragṛhya tu nistriṃśaṃ kālārkānalasaṃnibham
english: "Then the god Mahādeva, the trident-bearer, who once struck out Bhaga's eye, taking up that sword, bright as the fire of doomsday's sun,"

sanskrit: trikūṭaṃ carma codyamya savidyutam ivāmbudam cacāra vividhān mārgān mahābalaparākramaḥ vidhunvann asim ākāśe dānavāntacikīrṣayā
english: "and raising his three-pointed shield like a lightning-laced cloud, that one of mighty strength and prowess ranged through manifold movements, brandishing the sword in the air, eager to make an end of the dānavas."

sanskrit: tasya nādaṃ vinadato mahāhāsaṃ ca muñcataḥ babhau pratibhayaṃ rūpaṃ tadā rudrasya bhārata
english: "As he roared his war-cry and loosed a mighty laugh, the form of Rudra grew terrible to behold, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: tad rūpadhāriṇaṃ rudraṃ raudrakarma cikīrṣavaḥ niśamya dānavāḥ sarve hṛṣṭāḥ samabhidudruvuḥ
english: "Seeing Rudra in that form and themselves bent on dreadful deeds, all the dānavas, exulting, rushed upon him together."

sanskrit: aśmabhiś cāpy avarṣanta pradīptaiś ca tatholmukaiḥ ghoraiḥ praharaṇaiś cānyaiḥ śitadhārair ayomukhaiḥ
english: "They rained down stones, and blazing firebrands, and other dreadful weapons, sharp-edged and iron-tipped."

sanskrit: tatas tad dānavānīkaṃ saṃpraṇetāram acyutam rudrakhaḍgabaloddhūtaṃ pracacāla mumoha ca
english: "Then that host of dānavas and its unfaltering leader, scattered by the might of Rudra's sword, reeled and swooned away."

sanskrit: citraṃ śīghrataratvāc ca carantam asidhāriṇam tam ekam asurāḥ sarve sahasram iti menire
english: "So wondrous and so swift was the sword-bearer's movement that all the asuras took that single one to be a thousand."

sanskrit: chindan bhindan rujan kṛntan dārayan pramathann api acarad daityasaṃgheṣu rudro 'gnir iva kakṣagaḥ
english: "Cleaving, piercing, crushing, slashing, rending and grinding, Rudra ranged through the throngs of daityas like fire amid dry grass."

sanskrit: asivegaprarugṇās te chinnabāhūruvakṣasaḥ saṃprakṛttottamāṅgāś ca petur urvyāṃ mahāsurāḥ
english: "Broken by the rush of the sword, their arms and thighs and breasts hewn through, their heads sheared off, the great asuras fell upon the earth."

sanskrit: apare dānavā bhagnā rudraghātāvapīḍitāḥ anyonyam abhinardanto diśaḥ saṃpratipedire
english: "Other dānavas, shattered and crushed by Rudra's blows, roaring at one another, fled to all the quarters."

sanskrit: bhūmiṃ ke cit praviviśuḥ parvatān apare tathā apare jagmur ākāśam apare 'mbhaḥ samāviśan
english: "Some plunged into the earth, others into the mountains, some fled to the sky, and others entered the waters."

sanskrit: tasmin mahati saṃvṛtte samare bhṛśadāruṇe babhau bhūmiḥ pratibhayā tadā rudhirakardamā
english: "When that great and most fearful battle had run its course, the earth, miry with blood, looked terrible to behold."

sanskrit: dānavānāṃ śarīraiś ca mahadbhiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ samākīrṇā mahābāho śailair iva sakiṃśukaiḥ
english: "Strewn with the huge bodies of the dānavas, drenched in gore, O mighty-armed one, it seemed like a range of hills clothed in flowering kiṃśuka trees."

sanskrit: rudhireṇa pariklinnā prababhau vasudhā tadā raktārdravasanā śyāmā nārīva madavihvalā
english: "Soaked through with blood, the earth then shone like a dark woman, faint with drink, her garments soaked in red."

sanskrit: sa rudro dānavān hatvā kṛtvā dharmottaraṃ jagat raudraṃ rūpaṃ vihāyāśu cakre rūpaṃ śivaṃ śivaḥ
english: "Rudra, having slain the dānavas and set the world once more under the sway of dharma, swiftly cast off that terrible shape, and the Auspicious One assumed his gracious form.

sanskrit: tato maharṣayaḥ sarve sarve devagaṇās tathā jayenādbhutakalpena devadevam athārcayan
english: "Then all the great seers and all the hosts of gods worshipped the God of gods with a hymn of victory of wondrous fashioning."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān rudro dānavakṣatajokṣitam asiṃ dharmasya goptāraṃ dadau satkṛtya viṣṇave
english: "Then the blessed Rudra, with all honour, gave the sword — still wet with the dānavas' blood, the guardian of dharma — into the keeping of Viṣṇu."

sanskrit: viṣṇur marīcaye prādān marīcir bhagavāṃś ca tam maharṣibhyo dadau khaḍgam ṛṣayo vāsavāya tu
english: "Viṣṇu gave it to Marīci, and the blessed Marīci to the great seers, and the seers in turn gave the sword to Vāsava."

sanskrit: mahendro lokapālebhyo lokapālās tu putraka manave sūryaputrāya daduḥ khaḍgaṃ suvistaram
english: "Mahendra gave it to the guardians of the world, and the world-guardians, my son, gave the broad sword to Manu, the son of the Sun."

sanskrit: ūcuś cainaṃ tathaivādyaṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ tvam īśvaraḥ asinā dharmagarbheṇa pālayasva prajā iti
english: "And they said to him, who was the first lord of men: 'You are the ruler of mankind; with this sword, dharma's very womb, protect the people.'"

sanskrit: dharmasetum atikrāntāḥ sūkṣmasthūlārthakāraṇāt vibhajya daṇḍaṃ rakṣyāḥ syur dharmato na yadṛcchayā
english: "'Those who overstep the dyke of dharma, for causes great or small, are to be kept in check by punishment apportioned according to dharma, never at random.'"

sanskrit: durvācā nigraho daṇḍo hiraṇyabahulas tathā vyaṅganaṃ ca śarīrasya vadho vānalpakāraṇāt
english: "'Reproof, restraint, fines heavy with gold, mutilation of the body, and — for no slight cause — death itself:'"

sanskrit: aser etāni rūpāṇi durvācādīni nirdiśet aser eva pramāṇāni parimāṇavyatikramāt
english: "'these, beginning with reproof, are to be reckoned the forms of the sword; and the very measures of the sword arise from the gravity of the offence.'"

sanskrit: adhisṛjyātha putraṃ svaṃ prajānām adhipaṃ tataḥ manuḥ prajānāṃ rakṣārthaṃ kṣupāya pradadāv asim
english: "Then, having appointed his own son lord over the people, Manu, for the protection of the people, gave the sword to Kṣupa."

sanskrit: kṣupāj jagrāha cekṣvākur ikṣvākoś ca purūravāḥ āyuś ca tasmāl lebhe taṃ nahuṣaś ca tato bhuvi
english: "From Kṣupa, Ikṣvāku received it, and from Ikṣvāku, Purūravas; from him Āyus obtained it, and then Nahuṣa upon the earth."

sanskrit: yayātir nahuṣāc cāpi pūrus tasmāc ca labdhavān āmūrtarayasas tasmāt tato bhūmiśayo nṛpaḥ
english: "From Nahuṣa, Yayāti, and from him Pūru obtained it; from him Āmūrtarayas, and after him King Bhūmiśaya."

sanskrit: bharataś cāpi dauḥṣantir lebhe bhūmiśayād asim tasmāc ca lebhe dharmajño rājann aiḍabiḍas tathā
english: "And Bharata, the son of Duḥṣanta, received the sword from Bhūmiśaya; and from him, O king, it passed to the dharma-knowing son of Iḍaviḍā."

sanskrit: tataś caiḍabiḍāl lebhe dhundhumāro janeśvaraḥ dhundhumārāc ca kāmbojo mucukundas tato 'labhat
english: "Then from the son of Iḍaviḍā, the king Dhundhumāra obtained it; from Dhundhumāra it passed to the Kāmboja, and thence Mucukunda received it."

sanskrit: mucukundān maruttaś ca maruttād api raivataḥ raivatād yuvanāśvaś ca yuvanāśvāt tato raghuḥ
english: "From Mucukunda, Marutta, and from Marutta, Raivata; from Raivata, Yuvanāśva, and from Yuvanāśva, then Raghu."

sanskrit: ikṣvākuvaṃśajas tasmād dhariṇāśvaḥ pratāpavān hariṇāśvād asiṃ lebhe śunakaḥ śunakād api
english: "From him, born of Ikṣvāku's line, the valiant Hariṇāśva; from Hariṇāśva, Śunaka received the sword, and from Śunaka in turn —"

sanskrit: uśīnaro vai dharmātmā tasmād bhojāḥ sayādavāḥ yadubhyaś ca śibir lebhe śibeś cāpi pratardanaḥ
english: "Uśīnara, the righteous-souled; from him the Bhojas together with the Yādavas; and from the Yadus, Śibi received it, and from Śibi, Pratardana."

sanskrit: pratardanād aṣṭakaś ca ruśadaśvo 'ṣṭakād api ruśadaśvād bharadvājo droṇas tasmāt kṛpas tataḥ tatas tvaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ paramāsim avāptavān
english: "From Pratardana, Aṣṭaka, and from Aṣṭaka, Ruśadaśva; from Ruśadaśva, Bharadvāja, from him Droṇa, and after him Kṛpa; and then you, together with your brothers, have obtained that supreme sword."

sanskrit: kṛttikāś cāsya nakṣatram aser agniś ca daivatam rohiṇyo gotram asyātha rudraś ca gurur uttamaḥ
english: "The Kṛttikās are the sword's lunar mansion, Agni is its presiding deity, Rohiṇī its lineage, and Rudra its supreme teacher."

sanskrit: aser aṣṭau ca nāmāni rahasyāni nibodha me pāṇḍaveya sadā yāni kīrtayaṃl labhate jayam
english: "Now learn from me the eight secret names of the sword, O son of Pāṇḍu, by ever proclaiming which a man wins victory."
